_ghi_chu: EN-ALL GĐ 7 — bản tiếng Anh của thanso_doi_chieu.json (giao điểm Pitago ↔ Chaldea). Ban biên tập viết, chờ người bản xứ duyệt.

source.ten: Hieuban editorial reference text (2026) comparing the Balliett–Jordan (Pythagorean) and Cheiro (Chaldean) traditions
source.luu_y: Draft written with AI assistance, shown by decision of the project owner. The two schools are two different cultural traditions; neither is a forecast.

13.pitago: Pythagorean numerology treats 13 as a lesson in discipline: steady work instead of shortcuts.
13.chaldea: Chaldean numerology reads compound 13 as a season of change: the old closes so the new has room.
13.cach_dung: The two readings meet here: renewal lasts when it comes with steady habits — clear out the old, then be patient with the new.
13.tu_soi: The last change you started — how long did you keep up a steady rhythm with it?

14.pitago: Pythagorean numerology treats 14 as a lesson in moderation: freedom comes with responsibility.
14.chaldea: Chaldean numerology reads compound 14 as a connecting current: meeting, exchanging, everything moving fast.
14.cach_dung: The two readings meet here: the more connections and opportunities you have, the more you need clear limits of your own.
14.tu_soi: What do you often say yes to and later find is too much?

16.pitago: Pythagorean numerology treats 16 as a lesson about ego: rebuilding after something old no longer stands.
16.chaldea: Chaldean numerology reads compound 16 as the tower of renewal: an old structure gives way to a truer foundation.
16.cach_dung: The two readings meet here: humbly listening to feedback early helps you adjust before you have to start over.
16.tu_soi: Is there a plan you are holding on to only because you have already put effort into it?

19.pitago: Pythagorean numerology treats 19 as a lesson in independence and in asking for help: it is easy to carry everything alone.
19.chaldea: Chaldean numerology reads compound 19 as the bright sun: effort that is seen and recognised.
19.cach_dung: The two readings meet here: self-reliance is a strength, and letting others pitch in is also a way of being recognised.
19.tu_soi: Which task this week could you do together with someone?
